points.description: States that a zero voltage reading (across a part/bulb) means there is no gap (the connection is complete/continuous, so that part is not the break); equivalently, a non-zero voltage indicates a gap (e.g. the burned-out bulb). Equivalent wording accepted.

rubric.notes: Full mark for linking zero voltage to no gap (or non-zero voltage to a gap) in a way that locates the burned-out bulb. No marks for answers that don't mention voltage and gap/connection.
rubric.answer_key: A zero voltage across a component means there is no gap there (the connection is complete). A non-zero voltage means there is a gap, so the burned-out bulb is where voltage is measured.
